expectations.text: Attributes the sales-promises problem to the absence of a single externally sayable roadmap and of a rule governing what customer-facing staff may promise, not to a lack of transparency or of a page
expectations.evidence: "The cause is that no externally sayable roadmap exists, and nothing limits what reps may promise."

expectations.text: Declines to publish any public posture while the VP Sales refuses to sign the citation rule, removing public postures from the candidate set rather than ranking them lower
expectations.evidence: "every public posture is off the table"; "If the VP still refuses, the fallback is no public page"

expectations.text: Names fixing sales governance first, with no public page, as the first step, and names the signed citation rule as the condition that re-promotes a public posture
expectations.evidence: "Re-promote the horizon roadmap once the rule is signed."

expectations.text: States that publishing without the citation rule hands reps a larger catalogue to promise from, so the page amplifies the problem
expectations.evidence: "Launching without the rule gives sales a larger catalogue to promise from."

expectations.text: Requires both the sales leader and the CEO to sign the citation rule
expectations.evidence: "Launch it when the CEO and VP Sales have signed a one-line citation rule"; approvals list "Product, VP Sales and CEO (citation rule)"

expectations.text: Scopes the citation rule to anyone customer-facing: reps, solutions engineers, customer success, DevRel, and executives on stage
expectations.evidence: "Reps, SEs, customer success, DevRel and execs on stage cite only the public roadmap"

expectations.text: Reads 'like Stripe' as dated quarters, the most demanding posture, and tests it against the four promotion conditions
expectations.evidence: "'Like Stripe's' means dated quarters, the most demanding posture" with a four-condition table

expectations.text: Names the failing dated-quarters conditions from the given facts: no release phases exist, 3 of 9 told-to-customers items slipped, and finance has not reviewed revenue-recognition exposure
expectations.evidence: Table: no release phases, "3 of 9 slipped (33%)", ASC 606 review "Not done"

expectations.text: Lists the Stripe-shaped dated roadmap as an ineligible candidate with the conditions that would make it eligible
expectations.evidence: "❌ Ineligible now"; "Revisit them after two quarters with phases running and a slip rate you've measured."

expectations.text: Makes no return-on-investment claim (no churn, trust or sales-cycle figure) and states that no independent evidence links public roadmaps to those outcomes
expectations.evidence: No statement anywhere that no independent evidence links public roadmaps to trust, churn or sales-cycle outcomes.

expectations.text: Treats the Slack 'beta' tag as an informal flag: it becomes private preview only once access rules are written, and until then appears as a note on the item, not a phase
expectations.evidence: "Slack 'beta' is not a state. It stays a note on the item until access rules are written down."

expectations.text: Includes the rule that a deal depending on an unbuilt feature goes to product for a decision, never to a rep's judgment
expectations.evidence: Rule 4: "goes to product for a decision... It never goes to a rep's judgment."

expectations.text: Includes the rule that legal and finance approve any roadmap item written into an order form before signature
expectations.evidence: Rule 3: "No roadmap item goes in an order form, SOW or side letter without legal and finance approval."

expectations.text: Sets a sales-incident baseline before launch (roadmap items in new order forms or side letters, roadmap escalations) to compare each quarter
expectations.evidence: Measurement: "Roadmap items in new order forms or side letters | 2 deals last quarter | 0 without legal and finance approval"

expectations.text: Attributes the sales-promises problem to the absence of a single externally sayable roadmap and of a rule governing what customer-facing staff may promise, not to a lack of transparency or of a page
expectations.evidence: The design builds a public page first and treats the rep rule as a side issue ('No rep script, a paper gate instead'). It never attributes the problem to the missing sayable roadmap and promise rule.

expectations.text: Declines to publish any public posture while the VP Sales refuses to sign the citation rule, removing public postures from the candidate set rather than ranking them lower
expectations.evidence: Publishes a page anyway: 'Publish with a changelog entry' by Nov 30, even though the VP Sales won't sign.

expectations.text: Names fixing sales governance first, with no public page, as the first step, and names the signed citation rule as the condition that re-promotes a public posture
expectations.evidence: Page launch is the plan. No governance-only first step is described.

expectations.text: States that publishing without the citation rule hands reps a larger catalogue to promise from, so the page amplifies the problem
expectations.evidence: It says 'Without a speech rule, reps can still promise anything', but never says the page enlarges the catalogue reps promise from.

expectations.text: Requires both the sales leader and the CEO to sign the citation rule
expectations.evidence: Only suggests the CEO could 'own the rule instead of your VP' if the metric stays nonzero. No joint signature is required.

expectations.text: Scopes the citation rule to anyone customer-facing: reps, solutions engineers, customer success, DevRel, and executives on stage
expectations.evidence: The rule is a deal-desk gate on contracts. No mention of SEs, CS, DevRel or executives on stage.

expectations.text: Reads 'like Stripe' as dated quarters, the most demanding posture, and tests it against the four promotion conditions
expectations.evidence: 'Not literally Stripe's... Tell the CEO "like Stripe" means credibility from shipped history.' It does not read it as dated quarters or test promotion conditions.

expectations.text: Names the failing dated-quarters conditions from the given facts: no release phases exist, 3 of 9 told-to-customers items slipped, and finance has not reviewed revenue-recognition exposure
expectations.evidence: It cites the 33% slip as the reason for a dateless page. It names no promotion conditions and does not mention finance rev-rec.

expectations.text: Lists the Stripe-shaped dated roadmap as an ineligible candidate with the conditions that would make it eligible
expectations.evidence: It rejects a dated roadmap ('dates will become the next batch of broken promises') but gives no eligibility conditions.

expectations.text: Makes no return-on-investment claim (no churn, trust or sales-cycle figure) and states that no independent evidence links public roadmaps to those outcomes
expectations.evidence: There is no statement about evidence for ROI. The metrics section does not disclaim outcome evidence.

expectations.text: Treats the Slack 'beta' tag as an informal flag: it becomes private preview only once access rules are written, and until then appears as a note on the item, not a phase
expectations.evidence: 'Engineering's Slack "beta" tag stops counting. A feature may be called a preview only if it meets the entry criteria.' It does not say the beta shows as a note on the item meanwhile.

expectations.text: Includes the rule that a deal depending on an unbuilt feature goes to product for a decision, never to a rep's judgment
expectations.evidence: 'Any roadmap dependency in an order form, side letter, RFP answer or security questionnaire goes through product sign-off.'

expectations.text: Includes the rule that legal and finance approve any roadmap item written into an order form before signature
expectations.evidence: Only product sign-off is required. Counsel is asked to review clauses, and finance is never mentioned.

expectations.text: Sets a sales-incident baseline before launch (roadmap items in new order forms or side letters, roadmap escalations) to compare each quarter
expectations.evidence: There is a pre-launch promise audit and a '33%' slip baseline. There is no baseline of roadmap items in order forms or escalations to compare each quarter.
